$comment: Checked-in coverage map for #3802 rule 2, produced by the #3803 phase-1 audit (2026-09-30, master 1f41157ca), landed by #3802. Key = source glob relative to the repo root. Value = the formal/ families whose spec models behaviour in that file, or the string "unmodelled" for a lifecycle/timing/identity/concurrency file that no family models yet. A row is ANY-OF: a PR touching a mapped file must also touch a formal/<family>/*.tla or *.cfg file for ANY ONE of the row's families, or carry a `TLA+ unaffected: <family> — <reason>` line in the PR body for any one of them. A row listing 4 or more families (a hub file such as the LSP client) is too coarse for file-level matching, so an unmet hub row prints a note and never fails; a row written as {families, anchors} (index.ts) instead gates only on the families of a lifecycle hook handler a changed hunk lands in, and prints a note for a change outside every handler (#3878). `unmodelled` entries print an advisory and never gate; they keep the gap visible. Every formal/<dir> must be listed in `families` and named by at least one row; a TLA lane that adds a family adds its row in the same PR. `notes` explains the non-obvious rows and the hot files deliberately left out. Paths were checked to exist on master at audit time.

notes.clients/installer/index.ts: Only the install lock (tryAcquireInstallLock, acquireInstallLock, assertOwnsLock, the generation heartbeat) is modelled, and only partly: file-locks has no heartbeat or ownership recheck (#3553). The rest of the installer is not lifecycle.
notes.clients/lsp/server.ts: The LSP service generation (captureLspServiceGeneration, lspServiceGenerationCell, #3755) is session-lifecycle's `svc` (one process counter; `perEvalSvc` is the pre-#3755 per-evaluation counter, `Mut3755GenPerEval`, caught by `FleetOwnersLive`), format-drain's ServiceGen and lsp-idle-reset's reset. The server registry table (idleEviction policy data, #3622) is not lifecycle.
notes.clients/lsp/client-registry.ts: ClientRegistry (#2372 slice 3) holds what moved out of index.ts: per-client retirement (retireClient, #3672), capacity and idle eviction (#3622) map to lsp-crash `Evict`, the dead-client respawn and breaker to lsp-crash `Crash`/`Acquire`, and `markDestroyed` plus the client half of shutdown to lsp-idle-reset's reset. The per-generation derived state it drops through hooks stays in index.ts.
notes.clients/lsp/index.ts: Per-client retirement (retireClient, #3672), capacity and idle eviction (#3622) live in clients/lsp/client-registry.ts since #2372 slice 3 and map to lsp-crash `Evict`; per-generation derived state (EWMA, aux inflight, write-timeout streak) is not modelled yet (#3672, #3584). applyWorkspaceEdit callers are unmodelled (clients/lsp/edits.ts).
notes.clients/agent-nudge.ts: The agent-advisories store (#3757, carried on /reload by #3777) belongs to session-lifecycle, which does not model it yet. The `_touched` accumulator is unscoped (#3758 class).
notes.clients/widget-state.ts: The widget's per-verb write guards and rows (`diagnosticsWriteGuard`, `runnerWriteGuard`, `widgetStore`): session-lifecycle's WG policy row (carry on /reload, /fork, /clone, /tree; reset on the other starts, #3589) and, in SessionLifecycleF1, the two-verb pipeline write, the tie the guards must admit (`>=`), the rows' carry across a fork and the late verb's fence (F1 of #3803). What `reconcileStaleWidgetFiles` leaves of a record whose findings it shed is store-freshness' StoreRetire `Retire`: kept as unfinished evidence (`retain`, #4625), not deleted (`drop`, `dropOnce`: violated). Idle eviction and the fresh snapshot that ends the mark are not modelled.
notes.clients/write-ordering-guard.ts: `WriteOrderingGuard.shouldWrite` drops a token below the last seen and admits a tie. SessionLifecycleF1's `MutWidgetTieDrop` (`>`) and `Pre555WidgetNoGuard` pin both directions (F1 of #3803).
notes.clients/session-lifecycle.ts: Primary/secondary classification and the #3662 gap classification (#3668, successor-pending marker): session-lifecycle's SecStart, SecBind, SecUp and SecRoleless decline a start in a primary replacement gap unless it is the named successor (`namedSuccessor`), and `MarkerExpire` is the 60 s TTL as a nondeterministic step (`markerTtl`: an expired marker declines nothing; F1 of #3803). The `session-successor-pending` degradation record and the clock itself are not modelled.
notes.clients/dispatch/fact-store.ts: review-graph-signatures' Extract is atomic, which assumes the #3746 private-store property; the pre-#3746 shared store is below its abstraction.
notes.clients/tree-sitter-client.ts: Wasm trap budget, per-input trap entries with first-trap identity, decay on success, batch-compile keys (#3673, #3706, #3731). Modelled by tree-sitter-trap-budget (#3829).
notes.clients/tree-sitter-shared.ts: The tree-sitter-trap-budget family models the client's trap budget (`TreeSitterClient`, `reportWasmAbort`), not this module's own latch: `_wasmAborted`, its timestamp, and the `_shared = null` reset in `markTreeSitterWasmAborted` are unmodelled.
notes.clients/fix-run-restore.ts: Whole-package fixer vs concurrent agent sibling edits: capture, the restore under pi's queue for the sibling after the target's hold is released, and the lock order against multi-path LSP edits (#3741, #3830). Modelled by dispatch-pipeline `SiblingRestore.tla`.
notes.clients/lsp/edits.ts: applyWorkspaceEdit under every path's queue (#3610) and the rename staleness capture (#3736, #3747, #3734). Modelled by lsp-rename-edit (#3826).
notes.clients/lsp-mutation.ts: bookkeepLspMutation decides authorship on both branches (#4131, #4187): the direct recordWritten asks for an advance the read guard grants only for a path the call licensed, and the bridge fallback sends the same provenance and call id, so read-guard's own-write (OwnCall/OwnWrite) and co-process (BridgeWrite) actions are its two branches. The server-initiated workspace/applyEdit caller has no tool call and therefore no license; the fallback's missing-bridge degradation and its fail-open lineage (#3763 residual) are not lifecycle. For session-lifecycle, the fallback captures the session at `lsp_navigation`'s execute entry and sends it as the entry's lineage, so the bridge fences it like the settled sweep (#3824); `BridgeLineage` is fenced and `BridgeExtNoLineage` is the accepted I4 residual of #3763. The LSP request and workspace edit are lsp-rename-edit's.
notes.clients/mcp/session.ts: MCP session refresh calls handleSessionStart (scope 'superseded'); session-lifecycle states the MCP host is out of scope, except as a stager and reader of the turn-end slot (`McpStage`, `McpTake`, #4943 R2).
notes.clients/dispatch/dispatcher.ts: The delta split of a dispatch (`filterDelta` keyed on `d.id`, and since #4629 on a cross-tool `findingKey` too, which the model leaves out: what is new, what is held back, what is fixed) is modelled by blocker-pending (#4484): its `heldBackBlockers` is the observation's blocking set that the delta calls not new, which the pipeline's record, clean text and clear read. The rest of this note is about the coverage notice, which no family models. `buildCoverageNotice` decides per dispatch whether the synthetic model-facing coverage notice is emitted; the decision is the session-scoped `coverageNoticeSeen` latch (kind + file + sorted server sets) with the `dedupe` push/pull axis. No formal family models a model-facing coverage-notice dedupe: `dispatch-pipeline`'s `latch` is the `(file, hash)` analysed/in-flight dedupe in `clients/pipeline.ts`, and `session-lifecycle`'s `dedupe` is the #2890 duplicate-start gate. The coverage notice is unmodelled at the TLA axis.
notes.clients/dispatch/pending-runner-findings: The deferred collect-later runner store (#3758/#3813): both readers (drain, commit gate's non-draining peek) apply the owned-admission fence (ownedByLiveSession), and requeueRunnerFindings carries entry.session, so a requeued answer stays fenced to its producer scope. Modelled by pending-runner-store (#3814, #3824); the producer's captured-scope fence composed with the real lifecycle transitions is session-lifecycle's `StoreRunner` writer (SessionLifecycleF1, F1 of #3803).
notes.clients/knip-client.ts: The four heavyweight analyzers stamp scannedAt at the top of their run body, before the first read (#3690); a joined run inherits the initiator's read stamp. That is store-freshness' Stamp = "start" rule. The knip lane drops a late result by design and its two-sample floor and memo are not modelled (turn-end-late-scan README, "What the model cannot see"); only the shared `HardFailureStamps` is.
notes.clients/dead-code-client.ts: The turn_end dead-code lane's late scan (#4117 round 2, #4120): the client's single flight `inFlight` is process-wide, so a scan parked by one session is joined by the next session's analyze (J1, `JoinedScanStale`); `HardFailureStamps` is set where a scan settles and never cleared at a session boundary. The lane itself is in clients/runtime-turn.ts, which stays at its three families: a fourth would make the row a hub (4 or more) and silence the gate for the whole file. Modelled by turn-end-late-scan; store-freshness keeps the Stamp rule.
notes.clients/hard-failure-summary.ts: `HardFailureStamps` (stamp where a scan settles, 30 minute expiry, success lifts), shared by the knip and dead-code clients. Modelled by turn-end-late-scan (`NoRespawnWhileStamped`, `StampAtTurn`, `BackoffUnread`).
notes.unlisted: Runtime files touched by the 151 audited PRs and deliberately not mapped (no lifecycle, timing, identity or concurrency behaviour): bounded-telemetry, cache-observability, complexity-client, dispatch/types, dispatch/utils/format-utils, install-diagnostics, lens-config, lsp/config, lsp/session-roots, lsp/wait-policy/capability-snapshot, module-report, path-utils, persistent-reverify, probe-home-state, project-diagnostics/types, project-lens-config, python-environment, read-expansion, review-graph-logger, tool-agreement, tools/module-report. Also deliberately unmapped because nearly every PR touches them for non-lifecycle reasons: clients/degradation-ledger.ts (the DegradationKind registry; touched by most runtime PRs for a record kind, never lifecycle behaviour); clients/latency-logger.ts (telemetry sink); clients/hook-budgets.ts (budget table (data); #2523 governs it); clients/dispatch/runners/** except its utils/availability-policy.ts and utils/runner-helpers.ts, which have unmodelled rows (runner outcome parsing; the fix-run restore seam is mapped at clients/fix-run-restore.ts); clients/dispatch/facts/** (pure extractors; their tree-sitter trap accounting lives in clients/tree-sitter-client.ts).
notes.clients/turn-end/delivery-holds.ts: The turn-end delivery holds (#3813): peek-then-commit, drain-then-restore and park-then-recheck, settled once after the cap against the kept prefix (the reach rule), fenced by isCurrentSession, with the cut-advisory park keyed by session (#4112). Modelled by turn-end-delivery-holds. The producers register their holds in clients/runtime-turn.ts (handleTurnEnd), which is deliberately not given this family: that row would reach four families and its gate would turn advisory (#3878).
notes.clients/test-runner-delivery.ts: Automatic test-runner delivery (#2366): the in-memory pending delivery, the persisted deliveryEligible marker and the record's generations. A delivery's identity is the generation that published the record's content, not the testRunGeneration launch high-water mark (#5259), and it is eligible once its host reports idle, at agent_settled or at a publish after it. Modelled by test-runner-delivery; the idle rechecks and provenance validation are not.
notes.clients/opaque-mutation-scan.ts: The pending opaque baseline of bash calls (OpaqueBaselineStore: one entry per tool-call id, retirement of an entry whose turn is over, the pending cap and its counted loss; #4137). Modelled by opaque-baseline-slot, together with the authority-ranked dispatch dedupe its recoveries feed (claimPipelineDispatch). The record site is clients/runtime-tool-call.ts and the take site and the dedupe are in clients/runtime-tool-result.ts, so those rows list the family too; the recovery itself (recoverOpaqueChangesViaGit, captureFileStats) is a stat or git read, not lifecycle. The per-session HEAD records and their serialized looks (headRecords, observeGitHead, serializeHeadLook; #4493) are modelled by lsp-server-content HeadMoveResync, with the resync of held documents they drive; HeadMoveHookBound models the hook bound around a look, the primary-first send and the join of every tool_call (#4493 r2).
notes.clients/deferred-runner-blockers.ts: The commit gate's judgement of settled collect-later runner answers (`judgeDeferredRunnerFindings`). The file only reads the store through the non-draining `peekSettledRunnerFindings`, which is pending-runner-store's `PeekRead`; admission and drain live in clients/dispatch/pending-runner-findings.ts. Freshness-then-policy is not modelled.
notes.clients/finding-delivery-gate.ts: The delivery gate stack (#1634): the freshness verdict of a cited path against an entry's stamp, then the disposition policy over both arms, then the render. Modelled by finding-delivery for the cascade's pending neighbour record (stamp at the read, gated by freshness, kept each turn; #4495, #4487) and for a cached scanner store (demote, dispositions over live and stale, strict anchor). The file itself holds the contract and the surface registry; the gate code is in clients/advisory-provenance.ts and the stack in clients/runtime-turn.ts and clients/turn-end/lanes/. Not modelled: the project-wide admission of a secondary session, weak-anchored marks and the rule policy, and the render caps.
notes.clients/git-guard.ts: The git guard's command classification and its writes into session state. The session latch lives in `RuntimeCoordinator` (`updateGitGuardStatus`, `markGitGuardCacheUnknown`, cleared by `resetForSession`); the latch's late writers are modelled as the `gitguard` kind of session-lifecycle's `stateW` and `debounce` writers (`StateWLate`, `Pre3759StateWUncaptured`, `DebounceCaptureAtTimer`), so the latch's reset rules stay as they are in clients/runtime-coordinator.ts. Not modelled: the persisted blocker record (`syncGitGuardRecord` writes it, with its owner sections in `carriedBlockers`) and this file's callers of the latch writer, `resyncGitGuardAfterRetire`, `retireInlineBlockerAndResyncGuard` and `markCacheUnknown`.
notes.clients/advisory-provenance.ts: The advisory scanners' `scannedAt` stamp (taken at runScan entry, before the spawn) is store-freshness' Stamp = "start" rule, listed as 'not committed' in its store map. The finding-path freshness verdict (`FindingPathFreshness`, `FindingMissingPolicy`, the mtime-versus-scannedAt classification) is finding-delivery's verdict: live, stale or missing against the entry's stamp, with the fail-open `unknown` arm left out of that model. The rest is pure evidence shaping.
notes.clients/turn-end/lanes/secrets.ts: The secrets lane gates the gitleaks and trivy-secret caches by freshness (`onMissing: "drop"`, an edited file is demoted), then applies dispositions over both arms. Modelled by finding-delivery's cached store (CachedGate = freshness, PolicyArms = both, Anchor = line); the stat budget and the fail-open verdicts are not.
notes.clients/turn-end/lanes/govulncheck.ts: The govulncheck lane gates its cache by freshness, then applies dispositions over both arms. The stale arm and the dispositions are finding-delivery's cached store; the lane's `onMissing: "demote"` (a deleted trace file never drops a CVE go.mod pins, #1622) is the MutCachedKeepMissing policy as a deliberate lane choice, so the model's missing-drop rule describes the secrets lane only.
notes.clients/diagnostic-dispositions.ts: The disposition marks and their line-hash anchor. The store's writes are file-locks' row; finding-delivery models what the anchor decides at the gate (a false-positive survives only while the flagged line's content is unchanged, Anchor = line) and that a mark made against the current content is applied over both arms.
notes.clients/read-bridge.ts: Out-of-band reads forwarded to io-bridge's `recordRead` as `evidence: "disk"`, the read guard's `recordRead`. read-guard models disk-evidence reads at the tool_result seam (`EvidenceAtResultHandler`); the bridge's own producer timing is not modelled, so a change here moves read-guard or declares it unaffected.
The worker entry only serves one gzip-stage request and skips a body whose semantic fingerprint is unchanged. The Stage action and the generation-gated promotion live in clients/gzip-stage-write.ts and clients/project-snapshot.ts; the fingerprint skip itself is not modelled.
notes.clients/memory-sampler.ts: The sessionCell turn-end sample (`recordMemoryTurnEnd`; `takeMemoryIdleGapMs` takes it) and its session reset. The nearest family is session-lifecycle, which models the session-key index (#4965, `LastMemberOwnership`), not this cell's write and take. Process-wide sampling cadence remains telemetry-only.
notes.tools/ast-grep-replace.ts: `ast_grep_replace` captures the coordinator's session at `execute` entry and hands it to the apply, which sends it as the bridge entry's lineage (#3763 item 4, #3824). Modelled as session-lifecycle's `bridge` writer (`BridgeLineage`).
notes.clients/turn-summary.ts: The run's turn summary collector: a session-scoped store `resetForSession` clears, written by `handleToolResult` and the deferred-format drain behind the handle each captured at entry (#3759 row 14). Modelled as the `summary` kind of session-lifecycle's `stateW` and `debounce` writers (`StateWLate`, `Pre3759StateWUncaptured`); the collector's content is not.
notes.clients/dispatch/integration.ts: The in-lane cascade (`computeCascadeForFile`: the passive snapshot's post-edit gate, the tier branch, the bounded silent-push wait, the fallbacks, the unconfirmed marker) is modelled by cascade-delivery's `Compute`. The row stays at three families: a fourth would make it a hub and silence its gate (#3878).
notes.clients/runtime-turn.ts: `handleTurnEnd`'s drains and the park of a cut advisory: modelled by session-lifecycle's `TurnEnd` (a turn_end drains only its own scope's work: `SecondaryTurnEnd` is master's open half of #3613 and #3758, `SecondaryTurnEndScoped` the proposed shape) and `park`/`ParkTake` (`ParkMerged`, `Pre4112ParkNoSessionKey`, `Mut4112ParkNoResetClear`, `MutParkNoFence`; the key and fence are also turn-end-delivery-holds'). The row is deliberately not given session-lifecycle: a fourth family would make it a hub and silence its gate (#3878). Its cascade sections (the registry peek, the pending and unresolved lines, the pending record) are cascade-delivery's `TurnEnd`, left off the row for the same reason.
notes.index.ts: The hook handlers in index.ts: an edit inside one (session_start, session_shutdown, session_tree, turn_start, turn_end, agent_end, agent_settled, tool_call, tool_result, context, context_with_system) gates on that hook's families only, found by `findHookRanges` in scripts/lib/tla-coverage.mjs from the post-image the diff names (#3878). An edit outside every handler (activation setup, helpers) prints a note and never gates. `context_with_system` is the pi 0.87+ request hook that sees the full transcript; `context` injects on a pre-0.87 host and defers on 0.87+ (#4631). `model_select` re-plans the active tool set for the new model (#4687); it maps to session-lifecycle, whose LZ memory store is what the plan reads.
notes.clients/dispatch/runners/utils/availabil: Availability latch state (`available`, cooldown, install attempts, trust and availability generations) changes on probes, cooldown expiry, installs, trust adoption and session reset; no family models it.
notes.clients/dispatch/runners/utils/runner-he: Shared runner availability and managed-verdict flights carry in-flight probes, cooldowns and generation-scoped accumulators across callers; probe settle, reset, trust adoption and expiry are unmodelled.
notes.clients/out-of-band-changes.ts: The look's per-root records and owed walks (both `BoundedFifoMap(MAX_ROOTS)`), the coalesced flight and its trailing pass, and the commit-before-publish order are modelled by disk-change-publisher (`Begin`, `Read`, `Commit`, `Next`; `NoLostChange`, `DemandServed`, `OneRestartPerInstall`). The FIFO eviction that loses a change is the accepted p3 B2a (`B2aEvictedInstall`, `B2aEvictedDeclaration`). Declaration-walk caps, unreadable subtrees, the HEAD baseline and the abort signal are not modelled.
notes.clients/disk-changes.ts: The publisher's sequence allocation before fan-out, awaited and isolated fan-out, the once-per-consumer failure record and the agent-only authorship write set are modelled by disk-change-publisher (`Alloc`, `FanOk`, `FanThrow`, `PubDone`; I2 to I5). The registry of subscribers and the per-origin policy are not modelled.
notes.clients/disk-change-subscribers.ts: Registration order (the diagnostics cache, then the LSP consumer) is the fan-out order of disk-change-publisher's `FanOk`; what a subscriber does with a change (the cache clock, the client restart, the watched-files events) and its settled-sweep drain latch are not modelled.
notes.clients/safe-spawn.ts: Per-child teardown flags and timeout, abort, output-cap, close and escalation timers form a spawn lifecycle; child events and kill paths are unmodelled.
notes.clients/installer/managed-tool-refresh.t: Managed-tool refresh has an in-flight slot, session budget reservation and resettable tap points; session start, reset, stamp cadence and concurrent callers are unmodelled.
notes.clients/bootstrap.ts: Analyzer bootstrap tracks resident clients, shutdown state, failure strikes, load attempts and a keyed flight; demand, session reset, shutdown and late build settlement are unmodelled.
notes.clients/project-trust.ts: Process-wide trust state and trustGeneration change on adoption at session_start and turn_start; availability, LSP and installer consumers read the generation, with no formal family.
notes.clients/deferred-lsp-work.ts: One deferred LSP work slot moves idle to armed or aborted; turn_end, work settlement, session start/shutdown and idle reset are its actors.
notes.clients/event-loop-hold.ts: A process-singleton hold map and re-armed timer change on hold/release, deadline reap, session reset and timer failure; the liveness machine is unmodelled.
notes.clients/recent-touches.ts: Cross-process recent-touch append/read state combines a global mtime/size watermark with a per-CWD cursor; turn/session readers and concurrent producers are unmodelled.
notes.mcp/server.ts: MCP auto-session state and its in-flight self-heal change on tool calls, successful session start and failed retry; the host lifecycle is unmodelled.
notes.clients/lsp/workspace-sweep-hold.ts: Workspace sweep holds, idle waiters and age-based reap change on LSP work completion, idle reads and session reset; modelled by lsp-idle-reset.
notes.clients/lsp/workspace-diagnostics-sessio: The diagnostics session clock (`_sessionStartedAt`), the bounded file-creation map (`_fileCreations`) and the all-files-changed watermark (`_allFilesChangedAt`) change on session start, file creation and eviction. The nearest family is store-freshness, which models a cache entry stamped against its file's mtime, size and dependency `scannedAt`; it does not model these three, so the file is unmodelled.
notes.clients/lsp/aggregation.ts: Language and auxiliary completion counts plus grace timers change as LSP promises settle, in `raceToCompletion`, the result-aware race over multi-client diagnostics collection. The nearest family is late-aux-drain, which models `touchFile`'s aux-grace wait and the `turn_end` drain of late publishes; it does not model this race or its counts.
notes.clients/message-end-attribution.ts: The two-slot stable/previous session attribution anchor rotates at session boundaries (`rotateMessageEndAttribution`, called from clients/runtime-session.ts) for late message_end telemetry. The nearest family is session-lifecycle, which models the session boundary but not this anchor or its rotation, so the file is unmodelled.
